key_insight: In head-to-head testing of open-source thigh muscle MRI segmentation tools, specialized domain-trained models performed best and were more reliable than foundation or general-purpose models.
clinical_relevance: Better muscle segmentation can improve MRI-based volumetrics, radiomics, and fat-fraction measures used in neuromuscular disease research and potentially clinical workflows.
method: Benchmarked 8 open-source segmentation tools on 3D thigh MRI volumes.
Tested across 3 base datasets and additional derived datasets.
Compared quantitative accuracy plus qualitative usability, including performance on pathological cases.
evidence_signal: The study found substantial performance variation across methods and datasets, with many algorithms losing accuracy on pathological scans.
watch_item: Results may not generalize well to underrepresented populations or disease patterns, so real-world deployment needs careful validation.
paper_title: Benchmarking open-source automated thigh muscle MRI segmentation algorithms
